A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same HELM study. Their main text, equations, tables, figures and appendices are readable and support matching content across relocations and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original property-prediction, generation, clustering and antibody-annotation results, together with tokenization, loss-weight and scaling experiments.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical evaluations and adds vaccine-degradation prediction, additional controls, alternative metrics and robustness analyses.

M1.justification: HELM retains the same codon hierarchy, hierarchical cross-entropy weighting and MLM/CLM procedures described in Section 3. The new codon-type embedding model is evaluated as a baseline; HELM itself is unchanged.

E1.justification: v2 adds the COVID-19 Vaccine dataset, comprising 2,400 sequences with degradation labels, to the six existing property-prediction datasets. The OAS pre-training data and original tasks remain. The length/GC analyses subdivide the existing iCodon data.

E2.justification: Appendix A.12 adds MLM and CLM comparators using separate codon-type embeddings with standard cross-entropy. The scaling comparison also gains XE controls at 50M and 100M parameters, whereas v1 compared only HELM sizes. Existing foundation-model, architecture and random-generation baselines remain.

E3.justification: v1 reports random 70:15:15 splits; v2 specifies published splits for four datasets and LinClust-based splitting at similarity 0.9 for the others. v2 also adds Pearson/R2 evaluation and defined length/GC subgroup protocols, and replaces the 20M/50M/100M scaling design with 50M/100M comparisons. Appendix A.3 retains the old splitting instructions, so the reported protocol revision does not establish that experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v2 adds codon-pair-bias analysis, iCodon length/GC robustness tests and a codon-type embedding control. Scaling now tests whether hierarchy remains beneficial against matched XE models, while the 20M case disappears. v1's gene-distribution validation plots are also removed. Synonymous clustering and the alpha ablation are retained despite relocation and renumbering.

E5.justification: Both versions' Appendix A.3 specifies averaging over three random seeds/splits. Neither adds confidence intervals, dispersion estimates or formal significance tests. The changed splitting design is covered under E3.

E6.justification: Tables 1–2 retain the original six-dataset scores and add vaccine results, including MLM XE 0.801 versus HELM 0.833. v2 adds CPB, Pearson/R2, robustness and embedding-baseline results. Entropy values change, including MLOS 1.62 to 1.28; scaling values also change slightly, including 100M HELM MLOS 0.665 to 0.664. The 20M results and gene-distribution plots disappear. Clustering, annotation and generation results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The codon-tree formalization, probability factorization, HXE equations and exponential weighting function are unchanged. No new theorem, proof or substantive mathematical derivation is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction extend the stated prediction coverage from six to seven tasks. The contribution list explicitly adds the curated pre-training dataset as a contribution. The central hierarchical-learning claim, generative claim and approximately 8% improvement claim remain.

C2.justification: v2 adds explanations for transfer from antibody to general mRNA through shared structural features and molecular interactions (A.13), and attributes length/GC failures to pre-training coverage (A.11). It replaces v1's optimal-model-size discussion with an argument that scaling does not substitute for hierarchy (A.8). These substantially expand the mechanism and applicability discussion; the Euclidean-space limitation remains.

D1.justification: v2 documents construction of the codon-type embedding baseline and adds a promise to release code, datasets and weights, without an access link establishing availability. It removes the 20M configuration and timing information. The revised scaling section reports both two weeks and 82 hours for 100M pre-training without reconciling them; most existing implementation details remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds references supporting codon-pair bias, LinClust splitting, vaccine degradation, RNA geometry and the new transfer explanations. Examples include Coleman et al., Steinegger and Soding, Wayment-Steele et al. and Xu et al. The main related-work organization and positioning of HELM remain stable.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and the main section sequence are retained. v2 moves the clustering discussion into Appendix A.6, rewrites the scaling discussion, reorganizes appendix headings and adds a reproducibility statement and focused explanations. Author/affiliation and conference-header text also changes.

P2.justification: Tables 1–2 gain a dataset column, Figure 2 is redrawn, and a CPB plot and several results tables are added. The clustering illustration and clustering/annotation tables move into the appendix. The scaling chart becomes a comparison table, while the timing chart and gene-distribution Figure 9 are removed. The author block and conference headers are reformatted.

improvement.justification: The new codon-type baseline and matched 100M XE comparison strengthen tests of the hierarchy's contribution, while subgroup evaluations expose performance boundaries absent from v1. These provide a useful net improvement. However, unreconciled split descriptions, conflicting training-time statements, overgeneralized robustness prose and removal of the curation-distribution evidence limit the gain in overall quality.
